title: A retired architect in Dicmo, Croatia, spent nearly 50 years collecting carved stones from his family’s land, and archaeologists now say they belonged to a lost 1,900-year-old Roman arch built for Trajan
summary_full: Archaeological excavations in Dicmo, Croatia, have revealed a stunning Roman triumphal arch dedicated to Emperor Trajan, believed to have stood for nearly 1,900 years. Božo Kokan's efforts in gathering stones from his relatives' land played a pivotal role in identifying this significant find. The site boasts intricate Roman architectural features and elements like the imperial eagle, along with signs of a larger Roman community, underscoring the area’s extensive historical narrative.
